corrected_answer:
For scenario variant 131, treat low compute utilization and near-saturated bandwidth as observations, not a diagnosis. Assume model, GPU, runtime, clocks, input distribution, tokenizer, sampling, and quality target are fixed unless randomized; report measured values with units and label estimates. First collect synchronized per-token and per-kernel traces: DRAM/L2/cache/interconnect bytes and bandwidth, bytes/token, weights versus KV/intermediate/copy traffic, FLOPs, occupancy, issue/idle time, launch gaps, barriers, synchronization, overlap, clocks, power, temperature, memory pressure, errors, correctness, and output-quality metrics. A roofline bound is only a consistency check against measured counters.

Falsifiable hypothesis: within a predeclared workload stratum, the suspected dominant mechanism will show its predicted counter signature, and its intervention will improve median and p95 time/token by at least 5% (or the declared endpoint) without changing quality/correctness or violating resource, thermal, and error guardrails. A traffic hypothesis must reduce the corresponding bytes/token and time; a launch or synchronization hypothesis must reduce gaps/waits without requiring lower traffic. Otherwise reject the attribution.

Use randomized, repeated reference/current/intervention trials with held-out prompts, varying batch size, sequence length, precision, cache warmness/reuse, and kernel implementation; stratify by workload and report confidence intervals. Control concurrency, affinity, clocks, input order, compilation, and warm-up, and record raw traces. Confounders include cache residency, allocator effects, contention, asynchronous sampling, counter multiplexing, clock throttling, thermal drift, and quality changes. Canaries must pass latency, throughput, correctness, quality, memory, power, thermal, and error guardrails; fail closed and roll back on breach or missing telemetry. Do not generalize beyond tested strata without new evidence; domain-expert review remains required.
